scopeReview: SPS-3.A.1–2: historical contact, colonial/imperial institutions and trade shape current culture, including creolization and lingua franca. Conditional mechanisms, coercion and local agency retained; no claim that all contact languages follow a mandatory pidgin pathway.
varietyReview: Trade-network map, institutional timeline, contact-language table and market/home-language bars; other original cases examine coercion, institutional influence without mass settlement, adaptation, forced cultural relocation, names, cross-domain variation and chronology. All five skills and varied difficulty/keys.
repetitionReview: Historical causal channels distinguish this set from3.4 diffusion-type identification. Chronology versus current prominence, institution persistence and functional language versus language origins test different inferences. No copied or numeric-only repeated questions.
referenceNote: Official scope plus primary linguistic scholarship/institutional context checked. Original hypothetical data/places/language labels, no quoted lesson text or external catalog additions. No independent human review claimed.

questions.correctOption: Frequent trade connections can support diffusion to a more distant place before a closer, weakly connected one.
questions.independentReview: Independently compared schematic distances75 versus√1300≈36.1 and contact ratio100/5=20. Earlier uptake at the farther port is compatible with stronger connections; no deterministic causal effect or settlement count follows.

questions.correctOption: Colonial schooling and administration can create durable language institutions that persist after political control ends.
questions.independentReview: Followed introduced school/court use into post-independence retention. The historical sequence supports institutional continuity rather than inferring universal home use or inevitable permanent dominance.

questions.correctOption: The case is consistent with creolization: sustained contact contributes to a community language rather than simple unchanged copying.
questions.independentReview: Distinguished the supplied first-language community outcome from unchanged source copying and code switching. Nativization is evidence in this hypothetical case, not a universal requirement that every creole must derive from a prior pidgin.

questions.correctOption: It serves as a lingua franca at the market despite not being the preferred home language of this sample.
questions.independentReview: Recomputed home totals60+40+0=100 and market10+10+80=100. L’s0/80 contrast supports a functional shared-language role under the supplied mixed-language trade context, not a claim that no trader can speak L at home.

questions.correctOption: Institutional power and coercion can shape cultural diffusion and suppress alternatives.
questions.independentReview: Classified mandatory institutional use and penalties as power mechanisms, not evidence of biological incapacity or wholly voluntary choice. Preserved the possibility of local agency without minimizing coercion.

questions.correctOption: Control of influential institutions can promote selected practices without mass settlement by the controlling population.
questions.independentReview: Used explicit institutional control rather than requiring a mass demographic relocation. This tests a possible channel of imperial influence without making a legal claim about a real territory or treating every trade relationship as domination.

questions.correctOption: People can actively reshape elements from different traditions into a new expression.
questions.independentReview: Compared retained rhythmic knowledge with an introduced material element and a newly formed practice. No real musical tradition or group is attributed a fabricated history; the case illustrates creative adaptation.

questions.correctOption: Forced migration can carry cultural practices, even though movement was coerced and conditions constrained their expression.
questions.independentReview: Separated the existence of cultural transmission from freedom of movement. The invented case supplies no real route, count or named tradition; no inference of consent or complete cultural uniformity is made.

questions.correctOption: Colonial legacies and later local choices can coexist in the current cultural landscape.
questions.independentReview: Tracked historical persistence and later community decisions as distinct layers. The conclusion does not assign a single present attitude from a name or fabricate a specific real renaming dispute.

questions.correctOption: One shared communication practice can facilitate exchange without making every cultural dimension converge.
questions.independentReview: Held market communication common while varying religious practice, demonstrating nonidentical cultural dimensions. Avoided assuming that lingua franca means a new creole, common first language or one religion.

questions.correctOption: Inland has the earliest documented occurrence; Port may have been a relay rather than the original source.
questions.independentReview: Independently ordered10<40<70 and separated current industry size from first recorded occurrence. Earliest surviving observation is not automatically proof of an ultimate unobserved hearth.
